questions.q: Surgical disc compression in PIVD is done by:
questions.exp: Surgical disc compression: total/hemi-laminectomy or laminotomy + discectomy. (Book p183)

questions.q: Indication for surgery in PIVD is:
questions.exp: Indications: worsening symptoms despite conservative Rx. (Book p183)

questions.q: Another indication for surgery in PIVD is:
questions.exp: Indications: bowel & bladder involvement. (Book p183)

questions.q: Massive central disc prolapse compressing multiple nerve roots is:
questions.exp: Indications: massive central disc prolapse compressing multiple nerve roots. (Book p183)

questions.q: Cauda equina syndrome in PIVD is:
questions.exp: Indications: cauda equina syndrome. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Structure involved in conus medullaris syndrome is:
questions.exp: Conus medullaris: spinal cord involved (nucleus of Onuf S2); cauda equina: spinal nerves. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Structure involved in cauda equina syndrome is:
questions.exp: Cauda equina: spinal nerves involved. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Presentation of conus medullaris syndrome is:
questions.exp: Conus medullaris: UMNL with LMNL features; cauda equina: LMNL. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Presentation of cauda equina syndrome is:
questions.exp: Cauda equina: LMNL presentation. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Both conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes show:
questions.exp: Both show: B/L symptoms, bowel & bladder involvement, saddle anaesthesia. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Paralysis in conus medullaris syndrome is:
questions.exp: Conus medullaris: symmetric, areflexic, flaccid paralysis. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Paralysis in cauda equina syndrome is:
questions.exp: Cauda equina: asymmetric, areflexic, flaccid paralysis. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Etiology of conus medullaris syndrome is:
questions.exp: Etiology: conus medullaris = injury at L1. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Etiology of cauda equina syndrome is:
questions.exp: Etiology: cauda equina = large disc prolapse below L1. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Knee reflex in conus medullaris syndrome is:
questions.exp: Knee reflex: conus medullaris = normal; cauda equina = lost. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Knee reflex in cauda equina syndrome is:
questions.exp: Knee reflex: cauda equina = lost. (Book p183)

questions.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome
questions.q: Ankle reflex in conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes is:
questions.exp: Ankle reflex: lost in both conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes. (Book p183)

questions.q: Sequence in pathophysiology of lumbar canal stenosis is:
opts: Spondylosis (OA of facet joints) → excessive bone formation → stenosis → neurogenic claudication
questions.exp: LCS pathophysiology: spondylosis (OA of facet joints) → excessive bone formation → stenosis of lumbar canal → neurogenic claudication. (Book p183)

questions.q: Lumbar canal stenosis classically presents with:
questions.exp: LCS ends with neurogenic claudication. (Book p183)

questions.q: Pain of lumbar canal stenosis decreases with:
questions.exp: LCS pain: decreases with flexion - sitting, leaning over, walking upstairs/uphill. (Book p184)

questions.q: Pain of lumbar canal stenosis increases with:
questions.exp: LCS pain: increases with extension - walking, standing upright. (Book p184)

questions.q: In neurogenic claudication, walking (upright):
questions.exp: Neurogenic: walking (upright) causes symptoms; vascular: relieves symptoms. (Book p184)

questions.q: In vascular claudication, walking (upright):
questions.exp: Vascular claudication: walking (upright) relieves symptoms. (Book p184)

questions.q: Claudication pain that starts in the back is seen in:
questions.exp: Pain starts in back: neurogenic; starts in calf: vascular. (Book p184)

questions.q: Claudication pain that starts in the calf is seen in:
questions.exp: Pain starts in calf: vascular claudication. (Book p184)

questions.q: Standing stationary in neurogenic and vascular claudication respectively:
questions.exp: Standing stationary: neurogenic causes symptoms, vascular relieves symptoms. (Book p184)

questions.q: Climbing upstairs in neurogenic and vascular claudication respectively:
questions.exp: Climbing upstairs: neurogenic relieves symptoms, vascular causes symptoms. (Book p184)

questions.q: Postural changes in neurogenic and vascular claudication respectively:
questions.exp: Postural changes: neurogenic = yes, vascular = no. (Book p184)

questions.q: Pulses in neurogenic and vascular claudication respectively:
questions.exp: Pulses: neurogenic = normal, vascular = abnormal. (Book p184)

questions.q: Age at presentation in lumbar canal stenosis is:
questions.exp: LCS: elderly; PIVD: young. (Book p184)

questions.q: Onset of disease in lumbar canal stenosis is:
questions.exp: LCS: slow & progressive onset; PIVD: acute. (Book p184)

questions.q: Pain on flexion in PIVD:
questions.exp: Pain on flexion: LCS decreases, PIVD increases. (Book p184)

questions.q: Spondylolisthesis is defined as:
questions.exp: Spondylolisthesis: slipping of 1 vertebra over another. (Book p184)

questions.q: Cause of spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Cause: trauma/fracture of the pars interarticularis. (Book p184)

questions.q: Radiological sign of spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Spondylolisthesis: beheaded scottish terrier sign. (Book p184)

questions.q: m/c site of spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Spondylolisthesis m/c site: L5-S1. (Book p184)

questions.q: Radiological sign of spondylolysis is:
questions.exp: Spondylolysis: scottish terrier with collar sign. (Book p184)

questions.q: m/c site of spondylolysis is:
questions.exp: Spondylolysis m/c site: L5. (Book p184)

questions.q: Meyerding classification is based on:
questions.exp: Meyerding classification: based on percentage of slip. (Book p185)

questions.q: Meyerding grade I spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Grade I: 0-25% displacement. (Book p185)

questions.q: Meyerding grade II spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Grade II: 26-50% displacement. (Book p185)

questions.q: Meyerding grade III spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Grade III: 51-75% displacement. (Book p185)

questions.q: Meyerding grade IV spondylolisthesis is:
questions.exp: Grade IV: 76-100% displacement. (Book p185)

questions.q: Meyerding grade V spondylolisthesis (>100% displacement) is called:
questions.exp: Grade V: >100% displacement (spondyloptosis). (Book p185)

questions.q: Back pain in spondylolisthesis:
questions.exp: Clinical features: back pain radiating to the lower limbs. (Book p185)

questions.q: Step sign in spondylolisthesis is:
opts: Step off over the spinous process on palpation of spine
questions.exp: Step sign: on palpation of spine - step off over the spinous process. (Book p185)

questions.q: Spondylosis refers to:
questions.exp: Spondylosis: degeneration of the spine (elderly). (Book p185)

questions.q: Spondylitis refers to:
questions.exp: Spondylitis: inflammation seen in ankylosing spondylitis. (Book p185)

questions.q: Inverted Napoleon hat sign is seen in:
questions.exp: Inverted Napoleon hat sign (in spondyloptosis). (Book p185)
